<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-pasta" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-pasta-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of pasta, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

summaries retain their original statistic, material, basis and censoring. Each source drawer identifies methods and overlapping samples. No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:pasta-c4c3ea8380f8:be652b965cbf"><summary>HMI pasta Pb reference · Pasta, as sold</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:pasta-c4c3ea8380f8:be652b965cbf"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI pasta Pb reference · Pasta, as sold. Pasta, as sold; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤3</td><td>12.3–28.1 (bounded)</td><td>300</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤3</td><td>10.9–28.1 (bounded)</td><td>300–600 (bounded)</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>42 reference units; 3 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>27</td><td>33%</td></tr><tr><td>Pourimani et al. 2026</td><td>12</td><td>33%</td></tr><tr><td>Shaikh et al. 2025</td><td>3</td><td>33%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for pasta, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>3 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li><li><a href="../sources/pourimani2026-iran-pasta-wheat-germ-metals" class="internal" data-slug="sources/pourimani2026-iran-pasta-wheat-germ-metals" data-no-cite-meta>Pourimani et al. 2026</a></li><li><a href="../sources/shaikh2025-mumbai-ready-to-eat-foods-voltammetry" class="internal" data-slug="sources/shaikh2025-mumbai-ready-to-eat-foods-voltammetry" data-no-cite-meta>Shaikh et al. 2025</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Method: hmi-pooled-reference-v2.</p><p>hmi-pooled-reference-v2:pasta-c4c3ea8380f8:be652b965cbf</p><p>The reference is computed by HMI from admitted evidence, not copied from a study baseline. It describes the evidence currently in this scope; it is not a worldwide or current-lot benchmark. Source, year and region filters do not change it. Different HMI scopes are not one common ranking.</p></details></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:pasta-3dbf120ec843:9fba4d2e2f1f"><summary>HMI pasta Pb reference · Pasta, as sold, dry weight</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:pasta-3dbf120ec843:9fba4d2e2f1f"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI pasta Pb reference · Pasta, as sold, dry weight. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Marzabadi et al. 2026</td><td>5</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for pasta, as sold on a dry weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/collumb2019-las-vegas-gluten-free-pasta-flour-elements" class="internal" data-slug="sources/collumb2019-las-vegas-gluten-free-pasta-flour-elements" data-no-cite-meta>Collumb et al. 2019</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach pasta

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach pasta comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Pasta, as sold from retail brand B had Zn higher at 5,600 µg/kg, against 900 µg/kg for retail brand A in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/shaikh2025-mumbai-ready-to-eat-foods-voltammetry|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shaikh U, Samant R · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shaikh2025-mumbai-ready-to-eat-foods-voltammetry">Quantitative Determination of Heavy Metals in Ready to Eat Food Products</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal for Multidisciplinary Research (IJFMR) 7(6), November-December 2025</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shaikh2025-mumbai-ready-to-eat-foods-voltammetry">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

## Processing, cooking and preparation

<a id="hmi-ing-016"></a>
<a id="how-do-specified-processing-or-preparation-steps-change-the-measured-metal-endpoints"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-017"></a>
<a id="how-do-derivatives-concentrates-extracts-and-fractions-differ-from-their-parent-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-018"></a>
<a id="do-changes-reflect-removal-redistribution-moisture-or-yield-change-dilution-or-altered-species-or-availability"></a>

Processed or prepared forms were compared only with unprocessed pasta in the same study and group. Pasta, cooked (PAHO) had lead lower at 4.63 µg/kg, against 12.3 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (pasta, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Forms differ in water content, so a per-kilogram difference is not by itself a measured removal or gain of metal.

<p class="hmi-mitigation-gap" data-mitigation-gap>No measured way to lower metals in this food is in the library yet.</p>

<a id="hmi-ing-023"></a>
<a id="what-effects-on-nutrition-yield-sensory-quality-stability-and-waste-streams-were-measured"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-024"></a>
<a id="what-costs-constraints-adverse-effects-or-failure-modes-are-documented-and-which-are-unknown"></a>

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/shaikh2025-mumbai-ready-to-eat-foods-voltammetry|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shaikh U, Samant R · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shaikh2025-mumbai-ready-to-eat-foods-voltammetry">Quantitative Determination of Heavy Metals in Ready to Eat Food Products</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal for Multidisciplinary Research (IJFMR) 7(6), November-December 2025</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shaikh2025-mumbai-ready-to-eat-foods-voltammetry">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.



<a id="sampling-and-testing"></a>
## Testing pasta for metals

<a id="hmi-ing-025"></a>
<a id="what-sampling-design-is-appropriate-for-the-ingredient-heterogeneity-lot-and-decision"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-026"></a>
<a id="which-methods-species-measurements-validation-evidence-and-reporting-limits-are-needed"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-027"></a>
<a id="what-can-a-certificate-of-analysis-or-non-detect-establish-and-what-remains-untested"></a>

Results depend on the method and its reporting limit. Reporting limits for lead ranged from 0.2 µg/kg (Pourimani et al. 2026) to 3,000 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food), so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup References identify the sources used in these answers. The Sources index preserves additional discovery links; inclusion there does not mean a source has been reviewed for this assessment. Corrections, completed searches, new direct evidence and changes in requirements should reopen the relevant answer.


<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Pasta FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-pasta" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-pasta" data-question="What heavy metals are found in pasta?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in pasta?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, monomethylarsonic acid, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, uranium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Se, B, Ba, Ca, Ga, K, Mg, Mo, Na, P, Rb, S, Sr, Ti and Tl in pasta, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-pasta" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-pasta" data-question="How do heavy metals get into pasta?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into pasta?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, pasta from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than pasta from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/shaikh2025-mumbai-ready-to-eat-foods-voltammetry|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shaikh U, Samant R · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shaikh2025-mumbai-ready-to-eat-foods-voltammetry">Quantitative Determination of Heavy Metals in Ready to Eat Food Products</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal for Multidisciplinary Research (IJFMR) 7(6), November-December 2025</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shaikh2025-mumbai-ready-to-eat-foods-voltammetry">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Pasta, as sold from retail brand B had lead higher at 800 µg/kg, against 600 µg/kg for retail brand A in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/shaikh2025-mumbai-ready-to-eat-foods-voltammetry|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shaikh U, Samant R · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shaikh2025-mumbai-ready-to-eat-foods-voltammetry">Quantitative Determination of Heavy Metals in Ready to Eat Food Products</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal for Multidisciplinary Research (IJFMR) 7(6), November-December 2025</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shaikh2025-mumbai-ready-to-eat-foods-voltammetry">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-pasta" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-pasta" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in pasta?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in pasta?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, pasta, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (2.8 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (12.3 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in EURO (6 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (57.5 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-pasta" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-pasta" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in pasta?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in pasta?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same pasta.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Pasta, cooked (PAHO) had lead lower at 4.63 µg/kg, against 12.3 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (pasta, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
